title: Erdos #25: Logarithmic density of congruence-sieved sets

problemStatement.plain: Erdos #25 asks whether every set obtained by avoiding one residue class modulo each modulus in a strictly increasing congruence sieve has a logarithmic density. The Lean file defines the sieve, proves basic density API facts, and reduces the open problem to natural-density existence as a sufficient condition.
whyMatters: Captures a subtle density-existence question for infinite congruence restrictions.
Keeps the formalization honest about false or vacuous finite-sieve shortcuts.

proven: `logDensity`, `LogDensityExists`, `logDensity_mem_unit`, and `logDensity_unique` set up the logarithmic-density API.
`CongruenceSieve` and `sievedSet` formalize the modulus/residue avoidance problem.
`finite_sieve_density_exists` is proved vacuously under an eventually-constant hypothesis that contradicts strict monotonicity.
`zero_in_sieved`, `small_in_sieved`, `sieved_set_nonempty`, `sieve_monotone`, and `sieve_monotone_set` give basic membership and monotonicity facts.
`erdos_25_via_naturalDensity` shows natural density existence would imply the desired logarithmic density existence.
open: `ErdosProblem25` remains open for general congruence sieves.
A meaningful finite-sieve theorem should use a finite list of moduli rather than an eventually constant strictly increasing sequence.
The file notes that a naive coprime-moduli positive-density claim is false without extra hypotheses.
knownResults.goal: Strengthen the sieve model around finite lists and convergent exclusion sums before attempting the full logarithmic-density conjecture.
